financials_interim.notes: Sanasa Development Bank PLC (SDB), a Licensed Specialised Bank, FYE 31 December. Single-entity -- 'Investment in Subsidiary' (Payment Services (Private) Limited / UPay, Rs.6,163,100) is explicitly disclosed as NOT consolidated because it is deemed immaterial (Explanatory Note 5) -- no Group column anywhere in this filing, entered as a single basis='GROUP' row per convention. Source: documents.source_id '52647' (already registered by the automated collector on 2026-08-13, reused directly -- 'Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026'). unit_scale='000' (Rs'000, as explicitly labelled). This entry uses the filing's SIX-MONTH CUMULATIVE ('For the Period ended 30 June') figures, consistent with the bank convention used elsewhere this session; the filing separately gives quarter-only columns (not used here). IMPORTANT EXTRACTION NOTE: the raw PDF text layer for the income statement's '2026'/'2025' column headers renders in a confusing order in some extraction passes; verified the correct figures using the properly-rendered table image AND the Segment Reporting note (page 9, whose column totals for interest income/PAT are unambiguous) as an independent cross-check -- both confirm profit_after_tax H1 2026 = 106,815 (matches the filing's own press release: 'Profit after tax hit Rs. 106.85 Mn'). Mapped per bank convention: revenue = 'Total operating income'. operating_profit = 'Operating profit/(loss) before VAT on financial services & SSCL' (628,662 H1 2026 / 633,332 H1 2025). profit_before_tax = 'Profit/(loss) before tax', AFTER VAT (345,972) and SSCL (58,289) on financial services (not separately stored). finance_costs/finance_income/current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per bank convention. short_term_borrowings left BLANK -- this filing discloses only 'due to depositors' and 'due to other borrowers' as liability categories, with no separate 'due to banks' short-tenor line to distinguish from long-term borrowings. long_term_borrowings = 'due to other borrowers' (18,053,995) -- this is treated as genuine interest-bearing debt (the Cash Flow Statement's financing-activities section shows 'Repayment of long term borrowing' and 'Increase/(decrease) in borrowing' against this same balance, confirming it is debt, not deposit funding). 'Due to depositors' (110,747,860) deliberately excluded. total_equity = 'Total equity' (14,911,222); shares_in_issue = 164,166,494 (per Shareholder Information note, page 11). EPS/NAV cross-checks both tie exactly: 106,815k/164,166,494 = Rs.0.65, matches disclosed Basic EPS 0.65 exactly; 14,911,222k/164,166,494 = Rs.90.83, matches disclosed Net Asset Value per share of Rs.90.83 exactly. capex = Purchase of PP&E (75,359) + Purchase of intangible assets (101,355) = 176,714 (positive magnitude per project convention). DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (not silently resolved): the filing's own press-release page 2 states 'Stage 3 ratio improved to 5.96% from 5.42%' -- but 5.96% is HIGHER than 5.42%, meaning the ratio actually DETERIORATED (worsened), not improved, per the bank's own Selected Performance Indicators table (page 10: Impaired Loans Stage 3 Net ratio 5.96% as at 30.06.2026 vs 5.42% at 31.12.2025). This appears to be a wording error in the bank's own press release, not a data error on our part -- the structured table figure (deterioration) is trusted over the press-release prose, per established project practice.

interim_updates.note_text: SDB Bank's Total Operating Income fell 2% YoY to Rs.4,557mn (from Rs.4,640mn) for H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026), driven mainly by 'Net fair value gains/(losses) on financial assets at fair value through profit or loss' falling 52% to Rs.133mn (from Rs.275mn) -- a Rs.142mn swing -- while Net Interest Income held broadly flat (Rs.4,037mn vs Rs.4,071mn, -1%). PBT fell a more modest 13% to Rs.224mn (from Rs.257mn), but PAT fell a much steeper 32% to Rs.107mn (from Rs.156mn) because the effective tax rate jumped to 52.4% from 39.4% -- Income tax expense rose 16% to Rs.118mn even as PBT fell, meaning tax alone explains roughly 19 percentage points of the ~19pp gap between the 13% PBT decline and the 32% PAT decline. On the positive side, the Impairment charge fell 9% to Rs.378mn (from Rs.416mn), and Personnel Expenses fell 5% to Rs.2,020mn (from Rs.2,124mn) on cost discipline, partially offsetting a 13% rise in Depreciation & Amortisation (Rs.372mn from Rs.329mn) tied to branch/IT investment (per the Segment note, non-current asset additions rose to Rs.176.7mn from Rs.40.6mn). By segment (page 9): the Banking segment's result fell sharply to Rs.1,926mn from Rs.2,720mn as its segment Net Interest Income fell 28% (Rs.2,181mn from Rs.3,048mn) on higher inter-segment funding costs allocated to it, while Pawning segment result more than doubled to Rs.322mn from Rs.142mn on strong growth in the pawning book (Rs.14.2bn gross loans at 30 June 2026 vs Rs.11.3bn at 31 December 2025, +25%). The bank's own press release states the Stage 3 (impaired loan) ratio 'improved to 5.96% from 5.42%' -- this is factually backwards: 5.96% is a HIGHER (worse) ratio than 5.42%, so asset quality on this specific net Stage-3 metric actually deteriorated slightly during H1 2026, not improved (Gross Stage 3 ratio also rose, to 11.82% from 11.34%), even though the NPL ratio the press release also cites (8.71% from 8.85%) did genuinely improve -- these are two different, non-identical asset-quality metrics, and the press release's 'improved' framing appears to conflate them.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for SDB, so no prior quarter (e.g. Q1 2026 / 31 March 2026) is available for sequential comparison. This entry uses the filing's SIX-MONTH CUMULATIVE figures rather than a discrete quarter, consistent with the bank convention used elsewhere this session; the filing's own quarter-only columns (also available) were not used. The Stage-3-ratio discrepancy between the press release and the bank's own indicator table is flagged above rather than silently resolved in either direction.
interim_updates.takeaway: Revenue and operating profit both fell only modestly (a normalising Treasury/FVTPL gains base, not a core-lending problem -- Net Interest Income held flat), but a jump in the effective tax rate (39.4% to 52.4%) turned a 13% PBT decline into a 32% PAT decline, which is the real story behind the headline profit drop. Segment-level detail shows the Banking segment weakening while Pawning strengthened materially on loan growth -- a genuine mix shift, not a uniform deterioration. The bank's own claim of an 'improved' Stage 3 ratio is not supported by its own performance-indicator table, which shows a slight worsening on that specific net-basis metric.
operational_highlights: Total Operating Income -2% YoY to Rs.4,557mn as Net FVTPL gains fell 52% to Rs.133mn (from Rs.275mn), while Net Interest Income held broadly flat (-1% to Rs.4,037mn)
PBT -13% to Rs.224mn but PAT -32% to Rs.107mn -- effective tax rate rose to 52.4% from 39.4%, the single largest driver of the gap between the PBT and PAT declines

Impairment charge -9% to Rs.378mn and Personnel Expenses -5% to Rs.2,020mn (cost discipline), partly offset by Depreciation & Amortisation +13% to Rs.372mn on branch/IT investment (non-current asset additions Rs.176.7mn vs Rs.40.6mn a year earlier)

Pawning segment result more than doubled to Rs.322mn (from Rs.142mn) on a 25% expansion of the pawning book (Rs.14.2bn vs Rs.11.3bn gross loans); Banking segment result fell to Rs.1,926mn from Rs.2,720mn on higher inter-segment funding costs

Press release claims Stage 3 ratio 'improved to 5.96% from 5.42%' -- factually backwards per the bank's own indicator table (5.96% is worse than 5.42%); the NPL ratio (8.71% from 8.85%) did genuinely improve, a different metric
NAV per share Rs.90.83 (up slightly from Rs.90.18); Total Capital Ratio 14.94% (comfortably above the 12.50% minimum) though down from 15.24% at 31 December 2025
key_drivers: Effective tax rate rose to 52.4% (H1 2026) from 39.4% (H1 2025) -- income tax expense grew 16% to Rs.118mn even as PBT fell 13%, explaining most of the gap between the 13% PBT decline and 32% PAT decline

Net fair value gains on FVTPL financial assets fell 52% YoY (Rs.275mn to Rs.133mn), the single largest driver of the revenue decline -- a Treasury/investment-book base effect, not a core-lending weakness

Pawning segment result +127% YoY (Rs.142mn to Rs.322mn) on 25% gross loan book growth is the standout segment strength, while the Banking segment result fell 29% (Rs.2,720mn to Rs.1,926mn) on higher inter-segment interest cost allocation
